BUILDPLAN: M-07 — Wave 0 (§3)

Scope (verbatim): Hono router with a generated route manifest (glob, never a hand-edited list), error envelope, list contract (`page/per_page/q/sort/filters` → `{data,page,per_page,total}`), pagination helper, **bulk selector type (ids *or* filter)**, `json_each` chunking helper, OpenAPI assembly from route definitions, `/api/openapi.json`, `/api/docs`. **The chunking helper's default pattern is S-3's verdict** — M-07 must not pick one before the spike answers (trap 11).

Amendment 6 fold (+3 h, already inside the estimate): `GET /events` discovery, people reads, file lifecycle, scoped tokens (AC-242 UI is M-29's) — plus the pinned semantics: pagination, `ETag`/`If-Match` optimistic concurrency, one error envelope, standard rate-limit headers, durable bulk `operation_id` results, OpenAPI as the single source for docs/CLI/SKILL.
§7 rule this ticket institutionalizes: **registration by glob, never by a hand-edited list.** `src/routes/_manifest.ts` is generated at build from `import.meta.glob`; no agent ever edits a central registry to add a route, and the OpenAPI document is assembled from route definitions, never hand-written.

File surface: `src/api/*`, `src/routes/_manifest.ts` (generated)

ACs: AC-105, AC-106, AC-108
Hours: 4
Workflow: inline-full
Shared files: none by ownership — but `src/routes/_manifest.ts` is **generated**, never hand-edited, and that rule is this ticket's to enforce for the whole fleet.
Deps: M-02, S-3 (the chunking-pattern verdict — do not pick a pattern before the spike returns)
Plan: filled in by delegator's plan phase

data.body: Plan phase: working against forgejo/master @ f18011187f70fb0476ad837fc7f038a95306bfee. S-3 verdict read from merged parent history: default bulk ID transport is one JSON parameter expanded with json_each(?).

Plan review art_01KZJM16YMF9MMAAM9CMTTMZFX returned FAIL (plan-level); all six major and five minor findings are triaged in the authoritative Cycle 1 Resolutions block. Architectural corrections: D1 CAS writes, enforced API/SSR route discriminator, generated CLI registry consumption, literal org-scoped people detail paths, and adapter-based middleware. # Model switch: Kimi → Claude (operator decision, 2026-08-10)

This ticket's delegator was running on **Kimi** (Kimi Code / Moonshot, 15x coding
plan). Atin's call on 2026-08-10: the output is not meeting the bar, and the
remaining tickets move to **Claude**. Recording the exact state at handover so a
fresh delegator can decide what to keep rather than guess.

## State at handover

Branch `mrq-8-api`, worktree `../Marquee-worktrees/mrq-8-api`.
**Nothing is committed** — `master..HEAD` is empty. This is the most-advanced of the
four branches.

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `src/api/bulk.ts` | 137 |
| `src/api/concurrency.ts` | 130 |
| `src/api/route.ts` | 128 |
| `src/api/errors.ts` | 127 |
| `src/api/manifest.ts` | 113 |
| `src/api/pagination.ts` | 99 |
| `src/api/rate-limit.ts` | 99 |
| `src/api/runtime.ts` | 78 |
| `src/api/list.ts` | 69 |
| `src/api/grants.ts` | 26 |
| `src/routes/_manifest.ts` | 26 |
| `src/api/ids.ts` | 13 |
| `package.json` | modified — adds `@hono/zod-openapi`, `zod`, `@scalar/openapi-parser` |
| `package-lock.json` | modified |

**1,045 lines, zero test files.** `trace:ac` blocks merge on uncovered `auto` ACs,
so the tests are in scope for this ticket, not a follow-up.

## ⚠️ This ticket is the one N-7 was blocking

`check:api` asserted **CLI-registry parity on every PR from Wave 0** while the CLI is
MRQ-36 / M-38 at Tier B rank 19 — unbuilt. As written, every PR this branch opened
would have failed on a registry no ticket has produced. Fixed on `master` in
`1507bff`: that half of the assertion now **skips with a printed notice until `cli/`
exists**, and the served-JSON / rendered-docs half runs from the first PR. **Rebase
before opening a PR** or the branch fails a check that no longer applies.

## ⚠️ Merge-boundary violation — resolve before this branch merges

`BUILDPLAN.md` §7 makes **`package.json` M-06-owned, with edits serialized through
the orchestrator**. This branch edits it, and so does `mrq-14-uploads` (adding
`aws4fetch`). Both carry a regenerated `package-lock.json`. Two branches editing the
lockfile conflict hard and the resolution is not mechanical. Route the dependency
additions through the orchestrator, or land one branch and rebase the other before
it grows.

## Verify these against the contract before keeping the code

- **F-18** — there is **one** send route: `POST /api/v1/events/:id/comms/send`, body
  `{selector, template_key?, subject?, body?}` with exactly-one-of enforced
  server-side. **No `/messages/send` alias** — `check:api`'s registry parity asserts
  it, and AC-250 names it explicitly.
- **N-3 / SPEC §4.2** — `/i/:uid.ics`, `/agenda.json` and the public SSR pages are a
  named allowlist against the "`/api/v1` prefix throughout" rule. Registry parity
  must treat them as allowlisted, not as drift.
- **AC-108** — list endpoints share one contract: `?page&per_page&q&sort&<filter>=`
  returning `{data[], page, per_page, total}`, with filter semantics **matching the
  UI's exactly**.
- **AC-105** — the SPA uses `/api/v1/*` and nothing else. No UI-only write endpoint;
  gate 8 checks this by replaying a full-loop session with network recording.
- **Trap 11** — D1's 100-bound-parameter cap. One chunking helper lives in M-07, and
  spike **S-3** selects the pattern (chunk at ≤90 vs a single `json_each` parameter).
  Do not invent a second helper here.

## Contract changes to pick up before continuing

The worktree is on a pre-`1507bff` commit. Rebase on `master` first — the adversarial
pass closed out on 2026-08-10 and touched the harness contract:

- **`check:api` no longer asserts CLI-registry parity on every PR.** That half skips
  with a printed notice until `cli/` exists (MRQ-36 / M-38, Tier B rank 19). The
  served-JSON and rendered-docs half runs from the first PR. Before this fix, every
  PR opened against `check:api` failed on a registry no ticket has built yet.
- `SPEC.md` §4.2 names `/i/:uid.ics`, `/agenda.json` and the public SSR pages as a
  deliberate allowlist against the "`/api/v1` prefix throughout" rule.
- `EVALUATION.md` §1.2 adds the e2e split-do-not-delete rule; §5 records the
  desktop-only admin SPA as a non-goal.
- `SPEC.md` §3.9 gives the Airtable row counts a refresh owner (the daily keepalive)
  and renders them "as of `last_sync_at`".

Full disposition of the adversarial pass — 8/8 BLOCKING, 22/22 FIX, 8/8 NOTE — is in
`sequence/research/contract-adversarial.md`.

## Resume Revalidation Cycle 2 (Claude fleet) — plan revalidated with four amendments

Revalidated against `forgejo/master @ 04900e3` (branch rebased there; the prior revalidation was against `203dfa4`). Master has since gained `1507bff` (adversarial pass closed), `c64a9ba` (MRQ-4 seed spine), `9e8b425` (event -> conference rename), `13d37eb` (venue map), `04900e3` (Claude-fleet handover + MRQ-58). The plan and its Cycle-1 resolutions stand. Four amendments:

**W1 — `check:api` becomes real in THIS ticket, superseding revalidation item V4.** V4 read the merged stub's `MRQ-9` owner label and concluded "no M-07 action; it stays a stub." The boot prompt's N-7 section (from `1507bff`) rules the other way and wins: M-07 owns the route registry and OpenAPI assembly, so M-07 implements the activation rule. A `check:api` that hard-fails on a CLI registry no ticket has built is a broken gate for every ticket after this one. Implementation: `scripts/checks/check-api.mjs` — the sanctioned `runStub` replacement path, which changes the package script's target without renaming the script — with the served-JSON / rendered-docs parity half live from Wave 0 and the CLI-registry half skipped-with-printed-notice until `cli/` exists. MRQ-9 still completes the full-loop Playwright network-recording half.

**W2 — the SPEC §4.2 allowlist is explicit in the parity check.** `/i/:uid.ics`, `/agenda.json`, and the public server-rendered pages of SPEC §2.1 are a named allowlist, never drift. Encoded as data in `check-api.mjs`, not as a loose regex.

**W3 — the conference rename does not touch this ticket's API paths.** `9e8b425` renamed UI copy, the hash route `#events/new`, and the `{{event.name}}` merge field. SPEC §4.2 and §9 still specify `/api/v1/events/...` for every API path, and `src/db/schema.ts` still carries `event_id`. M-07's Amendment 7 contracts therefore keep `events` in their paths; renaming them would break the very contract this ticket exists to freeze. Flagging in case the Orchestrator intends the noun change to reach the wire surface — if so that is a SPEC amendment, not a delegator edit.

**W4 — inherited WIP judged, not trusted.** The prior session left 1,045 lines across `src/api/*` and `src/routes/_manifest.ts`, committed as-is first so the diff on top is legible. Baseline is red: three TypeScript errors (`errors.ts:126` implicit any, `runtime.ts:38` unconstrained env generic, `_manifest.ts:18` missing `import.meta.glob` types) plus a real defect in `buildManifest` — duplicate-route and duplicate-operationId diagnostics pass `entry.path` where the module path belongs, so the failure names a URL instead of the file to fix, which is exactly the diagnostic the plan requires. Zero tests shipped. Segments C, D, and E of the R6 order are entirely absent (OpenAPI assembly, both meta routes, Amendment 7 contract exports, verification). Fixing and completing, not preserving.

No other drift: the S-3 verdict is merged as assumed; `13d37eb`'s `buildings` table adds no column this ticket reads (lat/lng/access_minutes are MRQ-58's, untouched); the M-06 command table, `pr-gate`, and `trace:ac --scope=merged` behave as the plan assumed.

# MRQ-8 code review — own-reviewer fallback (quota directive)

**Reviewed commit:** `35953082ce9144d2543e6ce005d2e2cfb952932c` (branch HEAD, `mrq-8-api`)
**Base:** `forgejo/master @ 04900e3`
**Diff:** 27 files, +2559 / −9
**Reviewer:** `agent:delegator-mrq-8` acting as own reviewer. Headless `lattice code-review` is suspended under the quota directive; the Orchestrator independently scans the diff before merging.

## Verdict: PASS-WITH-NITS

The substrate is coherent, typed end to end, and proved on the real built artifact rather than on a hand-assembled fixture. Two nits and three deliberately-named gaps, none of which block merge.

## What was inherited versus what is new

The prior session's 1,045 uncommitted lines were committed first (`94e4562`) so the diff on top reads as a review. That baseline did not compile — three TypeScript errors — and carried one real defect. Everything after `94e4562` is this session's.

### Defect found in the inherited code (fixed)

`buildManifest` raised its duplicate-route and duplicate-operationId diagnostics with `entry.path` in the `modulePath` slot. A collision therefore reported `"/api/v1/dupe: duplicate route GET /api/v1/dupe (also declared by listDupes)"` — a URL and an operation id, neither of which is a file anyone can open. The plan's requirement is a diagnostic *naming the module*. Fixed by threading `{ modulePath, entry }` through discovery so both sides of a collision name their file; regression-tested at `tests/unit/api/manifest.test.ts:79` and `:89`.

## Findings

**N1 (nit) — `assembleApiDocument` takes `entries` only to compute signatures.**
`src/api/openapi.ts:112`. The document comes from `app`, the signatures from `entries`; nothing enforces that the two describe the same set at that seam. It is proved equal by test (`manifest.test.ts:119`) and by `check:api`, so this is a shape preference, not a defect. Left as is because collapsing it would mean re-deriving signatures from the generated document, which would make the parity assertion tautological — the two independent derivations are the point.

**N2 (nit) — `requireIfMatch` accepts a single strong tag only.**
`src/api/concurrency.ts:36`. RFC 9110 permits `If-Match: *` and a comma-separated list. Both are rejected with a 400 that says exactly why. For an optimistic-concurrency API where the client just read the resource, one tag is the honest contract and `*` is a footgun; a caller sending a list gets a precise error rather than a silent wrong branch. Deliberate, and documented in the function's doc comment.

## What was verified, and how

- **Real artifact, not a mock.** `check:api` imports the built Worker bundle (`dist/marquee/index.js`) and serves `/api/openapi.json` and `/api/docs` through the actual Hono app, then digests the bytes it received. The integration tests do the same through `SELF` in the Workers runtime. Neither path constructs an app by hand.
- **The digest chain closes.** Served body → SHA-256 → response `ETag` → the `marquee-openapi-sha256` meta tag in the rendered docs. All three are asserted equal in `tests/integration/api/meta.test.ts:37` and again in `check:api`. A docs page rendered from a stale document fails both.
- **Document validity** is asserted with `@scalar/openapi-parser` against the served bytes, and pinned at OpenAPI **3.1** (R7's condition is met: `@hono/zod-openapi@1.5.2` ships `getOpenAPI31Document`).
- **Registration cannot be hand-maintained.** `manifest.test.ts:140` asserts `_manifest.ts` imports exactly one module, contains the literal glob, and names no route; that `src/index.ts` contains no route registration; and that `router.ts` imports nothing from `src/routes/`.
- **S-3 is asserted behaviourally, not just by outcome** — one `JSON.stringify`, one `prepare`, one `.run()`, at both 150 and 1,000 ids, plus a source assertion that the helper never emits `?, ?` expansion or chunk slicing.

## Gate

`npm run pr-gate -- --ticket MRQ-8` → **pass**, 7,020 ms, all seven checks green.
Fast suite 4.5 s against a 30 s budget; `trace:ac --scope=merged --ticket=MRQ-8` reports 0 uncovered, 0 errors.

## Named gaps (in the PR body, not hidden)

1. **`dist/` registry emission (R3)** — cut under the capacity directive. `check:api` reads the built Worker directly instead of an emitted `dist/api-registry.json`, which is strictly more truthful for the served half; M-38 will still want the emitted artifact for offline `--help`, and `check:api` already has the branch that consumes it.
2. **Amendment 7 contract exports** (`src/api/contracts/*`) — cut. The primitives every one of those contracts composes from (list, pagination, bulk selector, CAS, rate policy, grants) all shipped; only the per-resource path/schema declarations are deferred.
3. **Full-loop traffic parity** — MRQ-9's half of the EVALUATION row, named in `check:api`'s own report under `notCoveredHere` so a green run cannot be misread as complete AC-105 coverage.

# MRQ-8 validation — the built Worker bundle, driven for real

**Commit:** `35953082ce9144d2543e6ce005d2e2cfb952932c`
**Artifact:** `dist/marquee/index.js` — the production `vite build` output, not the dev tree.

Green unit tests do not prove a Worker boots. So the artifact under test here is the shipped bundle, loaded and driven directly; no dev-only env var, no seed function, no in-process mock of the app.

```
GET /api/openapi.json -> 200 application/json
                         etag="70a8ec362ac91fe3a188f0d2c67463929dc9576fabcb5ca857f81886666e9313"
                         RateLimit-Limit=600 RateLimit-Remaining=600
GET /api/docs         -> 200 text/html; charset=UTF-8   (3,333 bytes)
GET /api/v1/does-not-exist
                      -> 404 {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"resource not found"},
                              "request_id":"5a7ea2bf-c9af-4035-b287-bf3b145a79c0"}
GET /health           -> 200 {"service":"marquee","status":"ok"}
```

What each line proves:

- **The document is served, valid, and self-describing.** `npm run check:api` re-fetches these same two endpoints from the same bundle, validates the body with `@scalar/openapi-parser` (reports `openapiVersion: "3.1"`), and confirms the `ETag` is the SHA-256 of the exact bytes returned. Report: `artifacts/checks/api.json`, status `pass`.
- **The docs render from the served document, not a copy.** The rendered page carries `marquee-openapi-sha256` = the served digest and an operation count equal to the document's. Both are asserted by `check:api` and by `tests/integration/api/meta.test.ts`. A docs page built from a stale document fails.
- **The unmatched-API 404 is the one envelope,** with a server-generated `request_id` echoed on `X-Request-Id`. The pre-existing ad-hoc `/api/*` 404 shape (which had no request id) is gone — misses now fall through to the API app's own not-found handler.
- **Standard rate-limit headers are on an ordinary success response,** not only on a 429, which is what the contract requires.
- **The API mount did not disturb the app.** `/health` is unchanged.

Additionally, `tests/integration/api/*` exercise the same endpoints inside the real Workers runtime via `SELF` (Miniflare), so the behaviour is proved on both the packaged bundle and the runtime that ships it.

## Not validated here

No browser or computer-use pass: M-07 adds no UI surface. AC-106's "linked from the running app's navigation" half belongs to M-29, which adds the sidebar link — this ticket ships the route it will link to.

Deployed-stack ETag preservation (R10's note that Cloudflare must not weaken the strong tag) is asserted locally only; it cannot be observed until a deploy exists.

Merged as PR #7 (squash c4e34037). Verified: head 3595308 != base, mergeable, secret/privacy scan clean, review+validation artifacts both naming HEAD. check:api is genuinely real — the N-7 activation rule is implemented (CLI half skipped-with-notice until cli/ exists; served-JSON/rendered-docs half live, validating OpenAPI 3.1 and asserting ETag == sha256(served bytes) == docs meta digest) and SPEC §4.2's three URLs are a named allowlist constant, not drift. AC-105/106/108 owned with tests/ac-claims/MRQ-8.json; trace:ac 0 uncovered. Cut and named: dist/ registry emission (R3) and Amendment 7 per-resource contract exports — neither blocks a downstream ticket since routes register by glob.
